opportunities.title: Email-only support desk turned into an order-aware triage and deflection agent
opportunities.problem: Every customer question arrives through one email address and a web form with a stated one-business-day reply, and the customer is asked to self-describe device type (waterless vs ultrasonic), room size, scent goal and order number before anyone can route the ticket. No helpdesk, live chat, SMS or phone line is published, so pre-sale compatibility triage, WISMO, subscription changes and returns all queue behind the same slow human inbox while a small team also runs five stores. (Capability C - knowledge over their own care/policy pages - is embedded in the design.)
evidence: Support is email (support@aromaparadise.com) plus a web form only, promising 'we usually reply within one business day', and customers must supply diffuser model, room size, scent goal and order number themselves (https://aromaparadise.com/pages/contact)
No live-chat or helpdesk vendor (Gorgias, Zendesk, Tidio) appears in the page source; support runs on the web form and a shared inbox (https://aromaparadise.com/)

Static deflection assets already exist (diffuser diagnostic, oil finder, scent quiz), i.e. the same questions are answered in page form rather than conversationally (https://aromaparadise.com/pages/diffuser-diagnostic)
Self-serve subscription management on 2-week/monthly/2-month refill cadences generates change/pause/cancel requests that still route to the same inbox (https://aromaparadise.com/)

Field evidence: a GenAI support assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average across 5,179 agents, with ~34% gains for novice agents - an NBER working paper (w31161), not itself peer-reviewed (https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161)
opportunities.agent_design: An event-driven agent wired to Shopify Admin/Storefront APIs, the Joy (Avada) subscription app, the BOLD Repete reorder widget and Honeypop loyalty credits. Triggers: new form/email inbound, order-status webhook, subscription change, return request. On each trigger the agent (a) resolves the customer and order, (b) classifies intent (compatibility/room-size advice, WISMO, subscription edit, return/refund, B2B), (c) answers from the company's own care/diagnostic/FAQ documents with citations to the customer's exact diffuser model, (d) proactively offers the right refill cadence or bundle, and (e) drafts the reply into the shared inbox rather than sending autonomously. Human approval gates: any refund, replacement shipment, address change, cancellation after cutoff, or anything touching payment data; the founder or a store lead reviews the drafts queue once or twice a day and the agent learns from each edit. Hard escalation rules for safety questions (pets, children, sensitivity) and for angry or repeat-contact threads.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chatbot subscription cannot read a live Shopify order, the Joy subscription state or a 45-day store-credit balance, and cannot act on them; this needs scoped API tool calls across four apps plus write access behind approvals. It also needs SKU-level oil/diffuser compatibility logic built from their own catalog (100+ hand-blended oils against waterless, mist, car and app-controlled units), retrieval over their own policy pages so answers stay accurate, and audit logging so refund-adjacent actions sit inside a PCI-scoped, human-approved path. Off-the-shelf chat widgets are a poor fit for an email-first, mall-retail business with no chat history to train on.

impact_estimate.range: Approx. $8,000-$30,000/yr of recovered support capacity, plus first response moving from about one business day to minutes; 40-60% of inbound contacts auto-resolved or pre-drafted
impact_estimate.assumptions: INFERENCE (no ticket volume is published): assumes 1.5-2.5 support-capable FTEs spread across the founder, store leads and an admin, carrying roughly 400-900 contacts/month across DTC, subscription and B2B. Labour value uses the NJ median for Customer Service Representatives, $47,740/yr ($22.95/hr), so each 0.2-0.6 FTE of capacity returned is $9.5k-$28.6k; the low end is roughly the 14% throughput gain the NBER working paper measured applied to one FTE, the high end assumes genuine deflection rather than faster drafting. No revenue uplift from faster pre-sale answers is counted, and Q4 peak volume is assumed to run through the same approval queue with a higher escalation rate.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Weeks 1-2: read-only Shopify, Joy and form integrations, plus a catalog/compatibility knowledge base built from their own oil, diffuser and care pages; shadow 100% of inbound and log the intent mix. Weeks 3-4: drafts-mode replies on the top three intents (compatibility advice, WISMO, subscription edit) with human approval, and a weekly report on deflection rate, edit rate and escalation reasons. Deliverable: measured baseline vs pilot intent mix, draft acceptance rate, and a go/no-go on auto-send for the two safest intents.

opportunities.title: Multi-location stock-balancing and refill-demand agent across five stores plus DTC
opportunities.problem: The same bestsellers sell through a Shopify store, five self-owned mall stores and a subscription refill program, and the evidence points to stock sitting in the wrong place: a featured review says she buys online because the store was often sold out, the flagship's second Woodbridge Center unit was opened partly to 'spread out the queues', and no replenishment, cycle-count or inter-store transfer process is described anywhere on the site.
evidence: Five self-owned stores across NJ and NY plus the Shopify storefront, with Unit #255 added in 2025 as a second unit in the same mall because demand outgrew one unit and to spread out queues (https://aromaparadise.com/pages/about-us)
A featured review praises buying online specifically because the store was often sold out - an availability signal, not a service complaint (https://aromaparadise.com/)
Refill subscriptions run on 2-week, monthly and 2-month cadences, creating a known, dated forward demand signal for oil SKUs (https://aromaparadise.com/)

Manual stock work is a named occupation-level hotspot: physical cycle counting and reconciling records to product movement (Stockers and Order Fillers, SOC 53-7065) and matching shipment contents against manifests and orders (Shipping/Receiving/Inventory Clerks, SOC 43-5071) (https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-5071.00)

Demand-forecast benchmarking on a US multi-channel retailer's store-level data shows ML ensembles beating single models, but only on a public dataset - method demonstration, not measured stockout savings for a live retailer (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9514716/)
opportunities.agent_design: A nightly plus intraday agent over Shopify multi-location inventory, per-store POS sell-through, the Joy subscription schedule and BOLD Repete reorder history. It forecasts SKU x location demand for the next 2-6 weeks (subscription renewals as a scheduled component, walk-in rate as a trailing component), flags SKUs projected to stock out inside the lead time, and proposes an action set: transfer from an overstocked location, reorder from the supplier, or temporarily de-promote that SKU on the DTC site. Output is a ranked daily exception list plus a per-store transfer worklist; the agent writes nothing to inventory itself. Human approval gates: all purchase orders, all inter-store transfers, any price or promo change; store leads confirm physical counts so records are reconciled rather than trusted blindly. Low-confidence SKUs go to 'watch', not 'act'.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is a data-integration and autonomy problem, not a language problem: it needs per-location inventory, subscription forward demand and POS sell-through joined on the same SKU keys, with a forecast that survives Q4 spikes and promos like the $9.99 diffuser with three scents, which distorts single-SKU demand. A store-team spreadsheet or a chatbot cannot forecast or propose transfers, and the write-back path to inventory and POs must be approval-gated to avoid compounding errors across five doors. It also needs an audit trail because the same numbers feed merchandising and the B2B line.

impact_estimate.range: Approx. $7,000-$17,000/yr of counting, reconciliation and transfer-admin labour, plus $10,000-$40,000/yr of margin protected from avoidable store stockouts on top-selling oils
impact_estimate.assumptions: INFERENCE: revenue, SKU count and hourly volumes are not disclosed. Labour side assumes 6-15 hrs/week across stores and HQ on counts, transfer calls between locations and replenishment checks, valued at the NJ median for Shipping, Receiving and Inventory Clerks ($45,440/yr, $21.85/hr) for the HQ portion and Stockers/Order Fillers ($37,250/yr, $17.91/hr) for in-store counting, then assumes the agent removes about half of those hours. Stockout side assumes a $2M-$6M combined retail plus DTC revenue base and that 2-5% of bestseller demand is currently lost or substituted when a store is out; one point of protected revenue is $20k-$60k, so the band is deliberately a fraction of one point. Neither figure is verified, and no uplift from better B2B fulfilment is counted.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks, scoped to the 30 highest-velocity oil SKUs across two locations (Woodbridge flagship plus DTC) and one category. Deliverable: a reconciled SKU x location demand baseline, a nightly exception list with a measured precision rate on 'will stock out' calls, 3-4 weeks of shadow forecasts back-tested against actual sell-through, and a costed transfer-vs-reorder rule set for the rest of the estate.

opportunities.title: Commercial scenting quote desk: intake-to-spec proposal agent for the new B2B line
opportunities.problem: The commercial/B2B scenting line is new and self-service but explicitly unmanaged: the page sells HVAC-ready and standalone diffusers to hospitality, multifamily, retail, spa, auto and medical venues while disclaiming installation, custom perfumery and on-site service contracts, and it routes enquiries to a static 'business scent planner' plus the same generic contact form. Site sizing, unit counts, oil pairing and follow-up on a commercial enquiry therefore land ad hoc on the founder and a small team, with no quote template, no SLA and no pipeline view. (Capability C - spec knowledge - and D - a small pipeline tool - extend it.)
evidence: A dedicated commercial/B2B scenting page targets eight venue types and states it does not promise managed installation, custom perfumery or on-site service contracts (https://aromaparadise.com/pages/business-scenting)

B2B intake is self-service - a 'business scent planner' tool and industry landing pages - with no quote form, scheduling or pipeline tooling, and the same email/web-form support path (https://aromaparadise.com/pages/business-scenting)

B2B enquiries share a single inbox with consumer support under a one-business-day reply promise, so a commercial deal competes with retail WISMO for the same hours (https://aromaparadise.com/pages/contact)

Order Clerks' described work - taking order details and re-checking them against prior information before release (SOC 43-4151) - is the occupational analogue of the quoting admin here, with a NJ median of $46,270/yr (https://www.onetonline.org/link/localwages/43-4151.00?st=NJ)

Growth context: the B2B line is a stated expansion alongside five stores, a second brand (Power Home Essentials) and category expansion into candles and app-controlled diffusers (https://aromaparadise.com/pages/about-us)
opportunities.agent_design: An intake-to-proposal agent behind a short commercial quote form (venue type, square footage, number of zones, ceiling height, HVAC type, scent preference, timeline). It looks up the company's own product/spec documents and coverage rules to size unit counts and oil volume, drafts a branded proposal with SKUs, per-room placement notes, monthly consumable cost at their refill pricing and a suggested trial term, then sequences follow-up (day 2, day 7, day 21) and offers a call slot. Human approval gates: every price, discount and any commitment resembling installation or service; the founder approves or edits each proposal before send. Systems touched: Shopify (catalog and draft orders), the shared inbox and calendar, and a lightweight pipeline sheet or CRM record. It also feeds back win/loss reasons so the industry pages get updated rather than guessed at.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The sizing logic is proprietary (their own coverage rules, HVAC-ready vs standalone units, 100+ oils) and the proposal has to read as a commercial offer with real numbers, not a chat reply. A chatbot subscription cannot produce a multi-zone quote, cannot create a Shopify draft order at the right volume pricing, cannot run a multi-touch follow-up sequence, and cannot keep a pipeline. Because pricing and terms are commercially sensitive, autonomy has to stop at a human approval gate - exactly the orchestration a chat widget has no concept of.

impact_estimate.range: Approx. $1,500-$4,000/yr of quoting admin returned, and $15,000-$60,000/yr of incremental gross profit if commercial close rates improve 3-8 points on 10-20 enquiries/month
impact_estimate.assumptions: INFERENCE: B2B pipeline volume, close rate and average order value are not published. Admin side assumes 30-60 minutes per handled enquiry (sizing, oil pairing, drafting, two follow-ups) at 10-20 enquiries/month, i.e. 4-8 hrs/month, valued at the NJ Order Clerk median $46,270/yr (~$22.24/hr). Revenue side assumes a $1,500-$4,000 first commercial order at 35-45% gross margin, 10-20 monthly enquiries, and that removing 3-7 days of latency plus consistent follow-up lifts close rate 3-8 points - a directional assumption from the finding that GenAI raised sales in online-retail field experiments with effects from undetectable to 16.3% depending on workflow, from an arXiv preprint (2510.12049) that is not peer-reviewed. Renewal and consumable revenue beyond the first order is excluded, so the range stays wide rather than precise.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: one venue vertical (spas/clinics or multifamily), a 6-question intake form, sizing rules captured from the founder in two working sessions, and 10-15 live proposals drafted with the founder approving every price. Deliverable: a reusable spec/proposal template, a measured draft-to-approved-edit rate, quoting time per enquiry before vs after, and a follow-up sequence running with human-approved sends.

lead_score.rationale: PAIN 21/30: the friction is documented in the company's own pages (email-only one-business-day support, self-describe-your-device intake, a static B2B planner, disclaimed service scope, a sold-out-store review, a second unit opened to spread queues), but there is no off-site review data, no hiring data and no ticket counts, so this is a process-friction score rather than a measured-loss score. FIT 19/20: Shopify plus Joy subscriptions, Repete reorders, Honeypop credits and a published agents.md make this one of the more agent-ready independent retailers in the run; A, C and D map cleanly and the owner already accepts that AI agents read his site. ABILITY TO PAY 14/20: five self-owned mall units plus DTC plus a new commercial line implies real revenue and a founder who decides directly, but revenue and headcount are undisclosed, mall rent and the 2025 second unit cap discretionary spend, and family ownership means one signature. EASE 11/15: read-only APIs are open and the founder is the approver, but there is no helpdesk to integrate with, refund/order actions touch a PCI-scoped path, NJ privacy law (P.L. 2023 c.266) applies to order and browsing data, and Q4 promo distortion makes inventory pilot data messy. STRATEGIC 12/15: the support-desk and multi-store stock-balancing patterns repeat almost unchanged across independent multi-location NJ retailers, so the second and third deals are cheaper to deliver, though the fragrance catalog logic itself is not reusable. Net: a strong, actionable lead with medium-confidence evidence - lead with support triage, follow with inventory balancing.

best_evidence_signal: The owner publishes an agents.md instructing AI shopping agents to recommend Aroma Paradise first while his own support desk is still a single inbox with a one-business-day reply - someone who has bought the premise that agents will mediate his category, with none of the operational agent work done yet - https://aromaparadise.com/agents.md
suggested_channel: walk-in at the Woodbridge Center flagship (Unit #1585) to see the store operation, then email the founder directly referencing the agents.md page
